# Every endpoint

Describes `main @ 5839d47`. Every answer each endpoint can give, with its cause and how to try it. How to read this: [README](README.md).

## Errors that can follow any call

Any of these can follow any endpoint below. They are not repeated under each one.

| Status | Code | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `MALFORMED_REQUEST` | The body could not be read as what the endpoint expects. |
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | No access token, or one that is expired or not valid. Everything under /api/v1 except the eight public auth POSTs needs one, and that is decided before the path is looked up: a path that does not exist, or a GET on a public auth route, is 401 without a token, not 404 or 405. A public route needs no token, but a token that is sent to one is still checked, and an expired or unaccepted one is 401 there too: send no Authorization header to a public route. In the account machine's own regions this answer is a row, because there the missing or expired token is the state. |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | A valid token that lacks the authority this action needs. |
| 405 | `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` | The path exists; this verb does not. |
| 406 | `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` | An Accept header that rules out JSON. There is no code of its own: it is the one a 415 carries. Read from the code; nothing runs it, and the contract documents no 406. |
| 415 | `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE` | A Content-Type this endpoint does not read. |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | The request parsed but a field or a required header is missing or not valid. |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | A rate-limit bucket is empty; Retry-After says when to try again. The buckets are kept in Redis and fail open: if Redis cannot be reached every request is let through, with no X-RateLimit headers, and nothing is 429 until it is back. |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Anything unanticipated. It never carries the underlying message. |

`401 UNAUTHENTICATED` is also a row in the regions `account` and `account.session`, where it depends on the state.

## Account

### POST /auth/register

register

**Needs:** no access token.

- Authorization (not needed, and best not sent: a token that is sent is still checked, and one that is expired or not accepted is 401 UNAUTHENTICATED before the request is looked at)
- Content-Type (application/json)
- X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (on answers, describing the bucket with the fewest left. Three registrations an hour per client address, one back every twenty minutes; the limit is spent before the body is checked, so a 422 uses one too. The fourth is 429 with Retry-After)

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X POST "$API/auth/register" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"email\": \"$EMAIL\", \"password\": \"$PASSWORD\", \"displayName\": \"Ada\", \"acceptedTermsVersion\": \"2026-09-01\", \"over18\": true}"
```

| `account` | `ANONYMOUS` |  | 201 → `PENDING_VERIFICATION` | The account is created PENDING_VERIFICATION, with its password hash and three consent rows, and a verification link good for 24 hours is emailed after the commit. The answer is 201 with an empty body and says nothing about the account. You are not signed in by registering. | FR-001, FR-011, ADR-0015 | test |
| `account` | `PENDING_VERIFICATION` |  | 201 stays | The address already has an account, so nothing is created, nothing is emailed and the password is not changed. The answer is the same 201 with the same empty body as a first registration, and a password hash is still computed so that it takes as long: the caller is deliberately not told the address is taken. A different case of the same address is the same address. | ADR-0015 | test |
| `account` | `ACTIVE_SIGNED_OUT` |  | 201 stays | The address already has an account, so nothing is created, nothing is emailed and the password is not changed. The answer is the same 201 with the same empty body as a first registration; the caller is deliberately not told the address is taken. The code does not look at whether the existing account is verified. | ADR-0015 | never-run |
| `account` | `SIGNED_IN` | no Authorization header is sent, or the access token it carries is accepted | 201 stays | The address already has an account, so nothing is created, nothing is emailed and the password is not changed; the answer is the same 201 as a first registration. Registering needs no access token and your sessions are untouched. | ADR-0015 | never-run |

Nothing is created. | smoke |
| 503 | `HASHING_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` | Password hashing is briefly full: six run at once, and a request that waits 250 milliseconds for a turn is answered 503 with Retry-After: 1. The request was fine; send it again. | test |

### POST /auth/verify-email

verify your email

**Needs:** no access token.

- Authorization (not needed, and best not sent: a token that is sent is still checked, and one that is expired or not accepted is 401 UNAUTHENTICATED before the request is looked at)
- Content-Type (application/json. The token travels in the body of a POST, never in a GET: a GET on this path without a bearer is the everywhere 401, so a mail scanner that fetches the link cannot spend it. No rate limit of its own)

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X POST "$API/auth/verify-email" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"token\": \"$VERIFY_TOKEN\"}"
```

### POST /auth/login

sign in

**Needs:** no access token.

- Authorization (not needed, and best not sent: a token that is sent is still checked, and one that is expired or not accepted is 401 UNAUTHENTICATED before the request is looked at)
- Content-Type (application/json)
- X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (on answers, describing the bucket with the fewest left. Two limits, both 429 with Retry-After and neither the lockout. Five attempts per fifteen minutes per email address as typed, one back every three minutes, counted for an address with no account too and spent before any password is checked: the sixth attempt is 429. And twenty an hour per client address. The lockout is separate and silent: five wrong passwords in a row lock the account for a minute, then longer, and a locked account answers 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS, not 429. With both in force the 429 comes first. The limits are kept in Redis and fail open: if Redis cannot be reached every request is let through and these headers are absent, while the lockout, which is kept in Postgres, still applies)

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X POST "$API/auth/login" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"email\": \"$EMAIL\", \"password\": \"$PASSWORD\", \"device\": {\"platform\": \"ANDROID\", \"appVersion\": \"1.0\", \"osVersion\": \"16\"}}"
```

An address that is not even shaped like one gets this answer too, not a 422. | FR-003, ADR-0020 §1 | smoke |
| `account` | `PENDING_VERIFICATION` | the account is not locked out and the password is right | 200 → `SIGNED_IN` | An account that has not verified its address may sign in. ### POST /auth/refresh

exchange the refresh token for a new pair

**Needs:** no access token.

- Authorization (not needed, and must not carry an expired token: a token that is sent is still checked, and one that is expired or not accepted is 401 UNAUTHENTICATED before the refresh token is looked at. A client that attaches its access token to every request must leave it off this one, or it cannot refresh once the access token has expired)
- Content-Type (application/json. The refresh token in the body is the credential. No rate limit of its own. Never send two refreshes of one token at once: the second is treated as a reuse and ends the session)

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X POST "$API/auth/refresh" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"refreshToken\": \"$REFRESH\"}"
```

#### Every answer

| Region | In | When | Answer | Why | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `account.session` | `NO_SESSION` |  | 401 `REFRESH_TOKEN_INVALID` | The refresh token matches none on record. Refresh needs no access token: the refresh token is the credential. Sign in again. | ADR-0021 §2 | smoke |
| `account.session` | `ACCESS_VALID` | you send the session's current refresh token | 200 stays | The token is exchanged: a new access token good for 15 minutes and a new refresh token good for 30 days, in the same session. The old refresh token is marked as used and must not be sent again. Nothing requires the access token to have expired first, and the one you held before is accepted until its own 15 minutes end. | FR-003, ADR-0021 §1 | smoke |
| `account.session` | `ACCESS_VALID` | you send a refresh token of this session that was already exchanged for a newer one | 401 `TOKEN_REUSE_DETECTED` | An exchanged token coming back means a copy exists: either a thief or the owner is holding a stale one, and the server cannot tell which. ### POST /auth/logout

**Needs:** no access token.

- Authorization (not needed, and best not sent: a token that is sent is still checked, and one that is expired or not accepted is 401 UNAUTHENTICATED before the request is looked at)
- Content-Type (application/json. The refresh token in the body is the credential. No rate limit of its own)

### POST /auth/forgot-password

Beside it, three an hour per email address as typed, one back every twenty minutes, counted for every address whether or not it has an account: the fourth is 429 with Retry-After)

```sh
curl -X POST "$API/auth/forgot-password" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"email\": \"$EMAIL\"}"
```

### POST /auth/reset-password

set a new password with a reset link

**Needs:** no access token.

- Authorization (not needed, and best not sent: a token that is sent is still checked, and one that is expired or not accepted is 401 UNAUTHENTICATED before the request is looked at)
- Content-Type (application/json. The reset token in the body is the credential. No rate limit of its own)

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X POST "$API/auth/reset-password" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"token\": \"$RESET_TOKEN\", \"password\": \"$PASSWORD\"}"
```

### GET /bonds

list your bonds

**Needs:** an access token.

**Try it:**

```sh
curl "$API/bonds" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

| `bond` | `NO_BOND` |  | 200 stays | You hold no bond, so the list is empty. An account that is not yet verified may ask too. |  | smoke |
| `bond` | `PENDING_MEMBER` |  | 200 stays | The bond is listed, newest first, with its live invite and its code. |  | smoke |

### GET /bonds/{bondId}

read a bond

**Needs:** an access token.

- If-None-Match (optional: the ETag you already hold. While what you would be shown has not changed, the answer is 304 with no body)

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -i "$API/bonds/$BOND" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

#### Every answer

| Region | In | When | Answer | Why | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bond` | `NO_BOND` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | There is no bond of yours under this id: you were never a member of it, it does not exist, or the id is not a UUID. One answer for all three, and never 403. | T-02, ADR-0026 §2 | smoke |
| `bond` | `PENDING_MEMBER` |  | 200 stays | The bond with you as its only member, its live invite, and its ETag. |  | smoke |
| `bond` | `ACTIVE` |  | 200 stays | The bond with both members, no invite, and anything waiting to be agreed. |  | smoke |
| `bond` | `PENDING_DELETION` |  | 200 stays | A bond counting down stays readable to both members, and says when it is scheduled to be deleted. | FR-028 | smoke |
| `bond` | `ARCHIVED` |  | 200 stays | An ended bond is a record both members keep. The member who left reads it too. | ADR-0026 §4, ADR-0028 §4 | smoke |

#### Whatever the state

| Status | Code | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | You are not a member of this bond, there is no such bond, or the id is not a UUID. All three get this one answer, and never 403, so that it does not confirm the bond exists. | test |

### PATCH /bonds/{bondId}

change the bond's settings

**Needs:** an access token.

- If-Match (required: the complete ETag of the bond as you last read it. The answer carries the new ETag; a patch that changes nothing keeps the old one)

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X PATCH "$API/bonds/$BOND" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "If-Match: $ETAG" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name": "Us two"}'
```

#### Every answer

| Region | In | When | Answer | Why | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bond` | `NO_BOND` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | There is no bond of yours under this id: you were never a member of it, it does not exist, or the id is not a UUID. One answer for all three, and never 403. | T-02, ADR-0026 §2 | smoke |
| `bond` | `PENDING_MEMBER` |  | 200 stays | The name, the type, the reveal time and Strict mode may be changed by either member alone, given the bond's current ETag as If-Match. The answer carries the new ETag. | ADR-0029 §1 | smoke |
| `bond` | `ACTIVE` |  | 200 stays | The same on a bond of two: either member may change these settings without the other, given the current ETag. Your partner's copy of the ETag stops matching. | ADR-0029 §1 | test |
| `bond` | `PENDING_DELETION` |  | 409 `BOND_ARCHIVED` | A bond counting down to deletion takes no settings change. The code is the one an ended bond gives. | BR-9, FR-028 | smoke |
| `bond` | `ARCHIVED` |  | 409 `BOND_ARCHIVED` | An ended bond is read only. This is answered before the If-Match is compared, so a stale tag gets it too. | BR-9, ADR-0028 §4 | smoke |

| 412 | `PRECONDITION_FAILED` | The If-Match you sent is not the bond's current ETag: somebody changed the bond since you read it, the tag is a weak one (W/"..."), or it cannot be parsed. Nothing is written. Read the bond again and retry. A bond that has ended or is counting down answers 409 BOND_ARCHIVED before the tag is compared. | smoke |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | The body names no setting at all; or names anchorTimezone, which only moves through /timezone with your partner's agreement; or name is blank or over 60 characters, type is unknown, or revealTimeLocal is not a time such as 21:00. | 428 | `PRECONDITION_REQUIRED` | No If-Match header, a blank one, or If-Match: *. The update must be conditional, so that two people editing at once cannot silently overwrite each other. It is checked after membership and before the bond's state is read. | smoke |

### POST /bonds/{bondId}/leave

**Needs:** an access token.

- Content-Type (application/json, and only when a body is sent. The body is optional and holds one key, {"withdrawEntries": true or false}: whether your own entries in this bond are taken back. With no body, no key, or null, a leave keeps them. Any other Content-Type is refused with 415, even with no body)

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X POST "$API/bonds/$BOND/leave" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"withdrawEntries": false}'
```

#### Every answer

| Region | In | When | Answer | Why | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bond` | `NO_BOND` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | There is no bond of yours under this id: you were never a member of it, it does not exist, or the id is not a UUID. One answer for all three, and never 403. | T-02, ADR-0026 §2 | smoke |
| `bond` | `PENDING_MEMBER` |  | 204 → `ARCHIVED` | Leaving a bond nobody joined ends it: it becomes ARCHIVED and its live invite is revoked. | `bond` | `ACTIVE` |  | 204 → `ARCHIVED` | One member leaving ends the bond for both: it becomes ARCHIVED, a record each of you can still read. | `bond` | `PENDING_DELETION` | you are still in the bond | 204 stays | Your membership ends and the bond goes on counting down: the deletion was agreed, and walking away does not undo that. ### POST /bonds/{bondId}/block

block your partner

**Needs:** an access token.

- Content-Type (application/json, and only when a body is sent. The body is optional and holds one key, {"withdrawEntries": true or false}: whether your own entries in this bond are taken back. With no body, no key, or null, a block takes them back. Any other Content-Type is refused with 415, even with no body)

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X POST "$API/bonds/$BOND/block" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"withdrawEntries": true}'
```

### POST /bonds/{bondId}/invites

issue a new invite

**Needs:** an access token.

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X POST "$API/bonds/$BOND/invites" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

#### Every answer

| Region | In | When | Answer | Why | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bond` | `NO_BOND` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | There is no bond of yours under this id: you were never a member of it, it does not exist, or the id is not a UUID. One answer for all three, and never 403. | T-02, ADR-0026 §2 | smoke |
| `bond` | `PENDING_MEMBER` |  | 201 stays | A fresh code is issued, good for seven days and one use. Any code still live is revoked in the same transaction, so there is never more than one. | FR-022, FR-023, ADR-0027 §4 | smoke |
| `bond` | `ACTIVE` |  | 409 `BOND_FULL` | Both members are in it, so there is nobody left to invite. | FR-022 | smoke |
| `bond` | `PENDING_DELETION` |  | 409 `BOND_ARCHIVED` | A bond counting down takes no new invite, whether it has one member or two. (a test asserts the status, not the code) | BR-9, FR-028 | never-run |
| `bond` | `ARCHIVED` |  | 409 `BOND_ARCHIVED` | An ended bond cannot be invited into. | BR-9, ADR-0028 §4 | smoke |
| `bond.invite` | `NONE` |  | 201 → `CREATED` | A fresh invite comes into being: a new code, good for seven days and for one use. Only a bond still waiting for its second member can issue one; the bond region has what the other statuses answer. | FR-022, FR-023 | smoke |
| `bond.invite` | `CREATED` |  | 201 → `REVOKED` | Issuing a new invite revokes the one that was live, in the same transaction, so a bond never has two working codes. The code you had already shared stops working at once. | ADR-0027 §4 | test |
| `bond.invite` | `ACCEPTED` |  | 409 `BOND_FULL` | The invite was used, so the bond has both its members and takes no new invite. Once the bond has ended or is counting down the answer is BOND_ARCHIVED instead: see the bond region. | FR-022 | smoke |
| `bond.invite` | `REVOKED` |  | 201 stays | A new invite is issued with a new code. This one stays revoked: a dead code is never brought back. | ADR-0027 §4 | never-run |
| `bond.invite` | `EXPIRED` |  | 201 stays | A new invite is issued with a new code. This one stays expired: a dead code is never brought back. | ADR-0027 §4 | never-run |

| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | You are not a member of this bond, there is no such bond, or the id is not a UUID. All three get this one answer, and never 403, so that it does not confirm the bond exists. | test |

**Needs:** an access token.

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X DELETE "$API/bonds/$BOND/invites/$INVITE" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

#### Every answer

| `bond` | `NO_BOND` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | There is no bond of yours under this id: you were never a member of it, it does not exist, or the id is not a UUID. One answer for all three, and never 403. | T-02, ADR-0026 §2 | test |
| `bond` | `PENDING_MEMBER` | the id is this bond's live invite | 204 stays | The code stops working at once. The bond stays as it is, with no invite until you issue another. | FR-023 | smoke |
| `bond` | `PENDING_MEMBER` | the id is not this bond's live invite | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | Already revoked, expired, another bond's, invented, or not a UUID: one answer for all of them, and nothing is changed. | FR-023 | smoke |
| `bond` | `ACTIVE` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | A bond of two has no live invite: the one that brought your partner was spent, and no new one can be issued. So no id names one. | FR-023 | never-run |

| `bond.invite` | `CREATED` |  | 204 → `REVOKED` | The code stops working at once, for whoever holds it. An invite is one-use but not tied to a person, so this is the remedy for a code that went to the wrong place. | FR-023 | smoke |
| `bond.invite` | `ACCEPTED` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | A used invite is no longer live, so there is nothing to revoke. Once the bond has ended or is counting down the answer is BOND_ARCHIVED instead: see the bond region. | FR-023 | never-run |
| `bond.invite` | `REVOKED` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | Revoking twice is not idempotent: the second call finds no live invite under that id. | FR-023 | smoke |

### GET /invites/{code}

**Needs:** an access token.

**Try it:**

```sh
curl "$API/invites/$INVITE_CODE" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

#### Every answer

| Region | In | When | Answer | Why | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bond.invite` | `NONE` |  | 404 `INVITE_NOT_USABLE` | A code that was never issued gets the one answer every unusable code gets, so guessing codes teaches nothing. (the test asserts the 404 and that the body is identical to the one accept gives a never-issued code; the smoke probe "a code that never existed is 404 too" asserts that body's code) | FR-024, ADR-0027 §1 | test |
| `bond.invite` | `CREATED` | you and the members of its bond have not blocked one another | 200 stays | You are shown the bond's name and type and who invited you, before anything is spent. Looking a code up leaves it live. Verification is asked for only on accept (read from the code; the caller in the probe cited is verified). | ADR-0027 §6 | smoke |
| `bond.invite` | `CREATED` | you and a member of its bond have blocked one another, in either direction | 404 `INVITE_NOT_USABLE` | A blocked person is not shown the bond's name and then refused: they get the same answer as for a dead code, so nothing tells them they were blocked. (the test asserts the 404 and that the body is identical to a never-issued code's; the smoke probe "a code that never existed is 404 too" asserts that body's code) | FR-029, ADR-0027 §3 | test |
| `bond.invite` | `ACCEPTED` |  | 404 `INVITE_NOT_USABLE` | A used code is not live. The answer does not say that it was once real, or that somebody got there first. (the test asserts the 404 and that the body is identical to a never-issued code's; the smoke probe "a code that never existed is 404 too" asserts that body's code) | FR-024, ADR-0027 §1 | test |
| `bond.invite` | `REVOKED` |  | 404 `INVITE_NOT_USABLE` | A revoked code is not live, whether it was revoked by hand, replaced by a newer one, or revoked because its bond ended or began counting down. | FR-024, ADR-0027 §1 | smoke |
| `bond.invite` | `EXPIRED` |  | 404 `INVITE_NOT_USABLE` | A code past its seven days is not live. It is a 404 and not a 410, which would say the code was once real. (the test asserts the 404 and that the body is identical to a never-issued code's; the smoke probe "a code that never existed is 404 too" asserts that body's code) | FR-024, ADR-0027 §1 | test |

#### Whatever the state

| Status | Code | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 422 | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | The code in the path is not six characters of the invite alphabet. It is upper-cased and trimmed first, so a lowercase code is not an error. This says nothing about any bond, which is why it is not the invite's 404. (the tests and the smoke script assert the status and the field, not the code) | never-run |

**Try it:**


### GET /bonds/{bondId}/members/me/settings

read your own member settings

**Needs:** an access token.

**Try it:**

```sh
curl "$API/bonds/$BOND/members/me/settings" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

#### Every answer

| Region | In | When | Answer | Why | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bond` | `NO_BOND` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | There is no bond of yours under this id: you were never a member of it, it does not exist, or the id is not a UUID. One answer for all three, and never 403. | T-02, ADR-0026 §2 | smoke |
| `bond` | `PENDING_MEMBER` |  | 200 stays | Your own reminder time and zone, quiet hours and nickname. Only yours: the path has no way to name your partner's. |  | smoke |
| `bond` | `ACTIVE` |  | 200 stays | Your own settings, as on a bond of one. Your partner's are never shown. |  | test |
| `bond` | `PENDING_DELETION` |  | 200 stays | Reading is not a write, so the countdown does not stop it. |  | never-run |
| `bond` | `ARCHIVED` |  | 200 stays | An ended bond's record stays readable, your own settings with it. | ADR-0028 §4 | smoke |

#### Whatever the state

| Status | Code | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | You are not a member of this bond, there is no such bond, or the id is not a UUID. All three get this one answer, and never 403, so that it does not confirm the bond exists. | test |

### PUT /bonds/{bondId}/members/me/settings

replace your own member settings

**Needs:** an access token.

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X PUT "$API/bonds/$BOND/members/me/settings" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"reminderTimeLocal": "20:00"}'
```

#### Every answer

| Region | In | When | Answer | Why | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bond` | `NO_BOND` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | There is no bond of yours under this id: you were never a member of it, it does not exist, or the id is not a UUID. One answer for all three, and never 403. | T-02, ADR-0026 §2 | test |
| `bond` | `PENDING_MEMBER` |  | 200 stays | All five fields are replaced: one left out is cleared, except the reminder zone, which is kept. No If-Match is needed, and the bond's ETag does not move. | ADR-0029 §6, §7 | smoke |
| `bond` | `ACTIVE` |  | 200 stays | The same on a bond of two. The row is yours alone, so the last write wins and your partner's view of the bond does not change. | ADR-0029 §6, §7 | test |
| `bond` | `PENDING_DELETION` |  | 409 `BOND_ARCHIVED` | A bond counting down takes no writes, your own settings included. | BR-9, FR-028 | smoke |
| `bond` | `ARCHIVED` |  | 409 `BOND_ARCHIVED` | Writes stop when the bond ends; reads do not. | BR-9, ADR-0028 §4 | smoke |

#### Whatever the state

| Status | Code | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | You are not a member of this bond, there is no such bond, or the id is not a UUID. All three get this one answer, and never 403, so that it does not confirm the bond exists. | test |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | reminderTimeLocal is missing or is not a time such as 21:00; one of quietHoursStart and quietHoursEnd is sent without the other; nicknameForOther is blank or over 40 characters; or reminderTimezone is not a region time zone. (the smoke script asserts the status and the field, not the code) | never-run |

#### The contract is silent on

| Status | What the code does |
|---|---|
| 415 | Any route that reads a JSON body answers 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE to another Content-Type; the contract's generator (OpenApiConfiguration.statusesFor) adds 415 only to the two Idempotency-Key routes. Read from the code; no test sends this route another Content-Type. |

### PATCH /bonds/{bondId}/timezone

propose a new time zone

**Needs:** an access token.

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X PATCH "$API/bonds/$BOND/timezone" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"anchorTimezone": "Europe/London"}'
```

#### Every answer

| Region | In | When | Answer | Why | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bond` | `NO_BOND` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | There is no bond of yours under this id: you were never a member of it, it does not exist, or the id is not a UUID. One answer for all three, and never 403. | T-02, ADR-0026 §2 | smoke |
| `bond` | `PENDING_MEMBER` | the zone has not moved in the last 30 days | 200 stays | Alone in the bond there is nobody to ask, so the zone changes at once and no proposal is written. Dates already decided are not redone: the new zone decides days from the end of the current one. | FR-027, ADR-0030 §8, BR-6 | test |
| `bond` | `PENDING_MEMBER` | the zone moved in the last 30 days | 409 `TIMEZONE_CHANGE_TOO_SOON` | The shared zone moves at most once in 30 days, also while you are alone in the bond. The detail names the date from which it may move again. | FR-027, ADR-0030 §7 | never-run |
| `bond` | `ACTIVE` | the zone has not moved in the last 30 days, and no zone change is waiting | 200 stays | A proposal is recorded for your partner to agree to within seven days. The bond's zone does not move yet, and the bond stays ACTIVE. | FR-027, BR-6, ADR-0030 §4 | smoke |
| `bond` | `ACTIVE` | the zone has not moved in the last 30 days, and a zone change is already waiting, yours or your partner's | 409 `PROPOSAL_PENDING` | The 30 days are asked first and the waiting proposal second. One zone change may wait at a time. The one that is waiting has to be agreed to, called off, or left to lapse before another is proposed. | ADR-0030 §3 | smoke |
| `bond` | `ACTIVE` | the zone moved in the last 30 days | 409 `TIMEZONE_CHANGE_TOO_SOON` | The shared zone moves at most once in 30 days. This is a 409 and not a 429: a month is not a rate limit. The detail names the date from which it may move again. | FR-027, ADR-0030 §7 | smoke |
| `bond` | `PENDING_DELETION` |  | 409 `BOND_ARCHIVED` | A bond counting down to deletion takes no new proposal. | BR-9, FR-028 | smoke |
| `bond` | `ARCHIVED` |  | 409 `BOND_ARCHIVED` | An ended bond's zone no longer moves. | BR-9, ADR-0028 §4 | test |
| `bond.proposal` | `NONE` | the bond is two people, and the zone has not moved in the last 30 days | 200 → `PROPOSED` | The first zone change this bond has been asked for. It is recorded with the zone it names and waits seven days for your partner; the bond's zone does not move yet. On a bond that has ended or is counting down the answer is BOND_ARCHIVED: see the bond region. | FR-027, ADR-0030 §1 | smoke |
| `bond.proposal` | `NONE` | you are alone in the bond, and the zone has not moved in the last 30 days | 200 stays | With nobody to ask, the zone moves at once and no proposal is written at all. | ADR-0030 §8 | test |
| `bond.proposal` | `NONE` | the zone moved in the last 30 days | 409 `TIMEZONE_CHANGE_TOO_SOON` | No proposal is written. With no earlier proposal, the zone can only have moved while you were alone in the bond, where a change applies at once. | FR-027, ADR-0030 §7 | never-run |
| `bond.proposal` | `PROPOSED` |  | 409 `PROPOSAL_PENDING` | One zone change waits at a time, whoever opened it. The database refuses a second as well, with a unique index. The 30-day rule is checked before this, but the zone cannot have moved while a proposal waits. On a bond that has ended or is counting down the answer is BOND_ARCHIVED: see the bond region. | ADR-0030 §3 | smoke |
| `bond.proposal` | `CONFIRMED` | 30 days have passed since the zone moved | 200 → `PROPOSED` | The last change was agreed long enough ago, so a new proposal is recorded and waits for your partner. On a bond that has ended or is counting down the answer is BOND_ARCHIVED: see the bond region. | FR-027 | never-run |
| `bond.proposal` | `CONFIRMED` | fewer than 30 days have passed since the zone moved | 409 `TIMEZONE_CHANGE_TOO_SOON` | The zone moved when the last proposal was agreed, and it moves at most once in 30 days. The detail names the date from which it may move again. | FR-027, ADR-0030 §7 | smoke |
| `bond.proposal` | `CANCELLED` |  | 200 → `PROPOSED` | A proposal that was called off is no obstacle: a fresh one is recorded, with its own id and its own seven days. On a bond that has ended or is counting down the answer is BOND_ARCHIVED: see the bond region. | ADR-0030 §5 | smoke |
| `bond.proposal` | `LAPSED` |  | 200 → `PROPOSED` | A lapsed proposal is invisible to every read but still holds the one slot, so proposing first stamps it cancelled and then records the new one. On a bond that has ended or is counting down the answer is BOND_ARCHIVED: see the bond region. | ADR-0030 §2, §3 | test |

#### Whatever the state

| Status | Code | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | You are not a member of this bond, there is no such bond, or the id is not a UUID. All three get this one answer, and never 403, so that it does not confirm the bond exists. | test |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | anchorTimezone is blank, or not a region time zone; a fixed offset such as Etc/GMT+3 is refused. A required field that is missing or null is not this answer: it fails while the body is read, which is 400 MALFORMED_REQUEST (by reading; nothing sends such a body). (the tests and the smoke script assert the status and the field, not the code) | never-run |

| 415 | Any route that reads a JSON body answers 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE to another Content-Type; the contract's generator (OpenApiConfiguration.statusesFor) adds 415 only to the two Idempotency-Key routes. Read from the code; no test sends this route another Content-Type. |

### DELETE /bonds/{bondId}/timezone

call off the time zone change

**Needs:** an access token.

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X DELETE "$API/bonds/$BOND/timezone" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

#### Every answer

| Region | In | When | Answer | Why | Rule | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bond` | `NO_BOND` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | There is no bond of yours under this id: you were never a member of it, it does not exist, or the id is not a UUID. One answer for all three, and never 403. | T-02, ADR-0026 §2 | test |
| `bond` | `PENDING_MEMBER` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | Nothing can be waiting on a bond of one, so there is nothing to call off. | ADR-0030 §8 | never-run |
| `bond` | `ACTIVE` | a zone change is waiting, yours or your partner's | 204 stays | Either member may call it off. The bond's zone stays where it was, and a fresh proposal may be made. | ADR-0030 §5 | smoke |
| `bond` | `ACTIVE` | no zone change is waiting | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | There is nothing to call off: never proposed, already agreed, already called off, or lapsed. (a test asserts the status, not the code) | ADR-0030 §5 | never-run |
| `bond` | `PENDING_DELETION` | a zone change proposed before the countdown is still waiting | 204 stays | Calling a proposal off takes nothing away, so it is not refused while the bond counts down. Starting the countdown does not itself cancel a waiting zone change. | ADR-0030 §5 | never-run |
| `bond` | `PENDING_DELETION` | no zone change is waiting | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | There is nothing to call off. | ADR-0030 §5 | never-run |
| `bond` | `ARCHIVED` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | Ending a bond cancels whatever was waiting, so nothing is left to call off. The answer is the 404, not BOND_ARCHIVED: this route does not look at the bond's state. (a test asserts the status, not the code) | ADR-0030 §5, §11 | never-run |
| `bond.proposal` | `NONE` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | Nothing has been proposed, so there is nothing to call off. This route does not look at the bond's status. (a test asserts the status, not the code) | ADR-0030 §5 | never-run |
| `bond.proposal` | `PROPOSED` |  | 204 → `CANCELLED` | Either member may call it off, the one who opened it or the other. The bond's zone stays where it was. It works while the bond counts down to deletion too, because calling a proposal off takes nothing away. | ADR-0030 §5 | smoke |
| `bond.proposal` | `CONFIRMED` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | It was agreed to and the zone has moved; an agreed change cannot be called off. | ADR-0030 §5 | never-run |
| `bond.proposal` | `CANCELLED` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | It was already called off, and calling off twice is not idempotent. (a test asserts the status, not the code) | ADR-0030 §5 | never-run |
| `bond.proposal` | `LAPSED` |  | 404 `NOT_FOUND` | It lapsed unanswered, which already has the effect of calling it off. | ADR-0030 §5 | never-run |

#### Whatever the state

| Status | Code | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | You are not a member of this bond, there is no such bond, or the id is not a UUID. All three get this one answer, and never 403, so that it does not confirm the bond exists. | test |

## Day

### POST /bonds/{bondId}/entries

write today's entry

**Needs:** an access token.

- Idempotency-Key (required. Repeating a key with the body it was first sent with is a replay: 201 again with Idempotency-Replayed: true, the entry as it stands now, and no entry written)

**Try it:**

```sh
curl -X POST "$API/bonds/$BOND/entries" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text": "..."}'
```

#### Every answer

| Region | In | When | Answer | Why | Rule | Evidence |

| `bond` | `PENDING_DELETION` | a new request | 409 `BOND_ARCHIVED` | A bond counting down to deletion takes no new entry, from either member. It is checked under the bond's lock and before the day is looked at, so nothing is stored and no day is opened. | BR-9 | test |
| `bond` | `PENDING_DELETION` | the request repeats an Idempotency-Key and body you already sent | 201 stays | A replay is a read of what your first request made, not a second write, so the bond's state does not refuse it: 201 again with Idempotency-Replayed: true and the entry as it stands now. | ADR-0031 §8 | never-run |
| `bond` | `ARCHIVED` | a new request | 409 `BOND_ARCHIVED` | A bond that has ended takes no new entry, from either member. It is checked under the bond's lock and before the day is looked at, so nothing is stored and no day is opened. | BR-9 | test |
| `bond` | `ARCHIVED` | the request repeats an Idempotency-Key and body you already sent | 201 stays | A replay is a read of what your first request made, not a second write, so the bond's state does not refuse it: 201 again with Idempotency-Replayed: true and the entry as it stands now. | ADR-0031 §8 | test |
| `day` | `NOT_OPENED` | the bond takes entries and is two people, and the day did not end before the bond became two people | 201 → `PARTIAL` | Yours is the first entry of the day, and this write is what opens the day's row. | `day` | `REVEALED` |  | 200 stays | The day is a COMPLETE square. While it is today it is added to the run at read time, provided the day before has been evaluated; after midnight the close job evaluates it and stores the same number. | FR-071 | smoke |
| `day` | `SOLO` |  | 200 stays | Once the close job has evaluated it, a day one of you wrote on is a SOLO square and is not in the run. It has no square if it moved nothing: missed after the bond had ended, or during a deletion countdown since called off. | ADR-0034 ruling 2 | test |
| `day` | `EMPTY` |  | 200 stays | Once the close job has evaluated it, a day nobody wrote on is a MISSED square and is not in the run. It has no square if it moved nothing: missed after the bond had ended, or during a deletion countdown since called off. | BR-4 | test |
| `day` | `FROZEN` |  | 200 stays | A rest day: a freeze covered it, or a zone change stepped over the date. It is a FROZEN square and it keeps the run going. | BR-5 | test |
| `day` | `SUSPENDED` |  | 200 stays | A suspended day has no square and moves no number. A bond still waiting for its second member has no calendar at all, whatever its creator wrote. | doc 04 §8.3a | test |

#### Whatever the state

| Status | Code | Why | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | You are not a member of this bond, there is no such bond, or the id is not a UUID. All three get this one answer, and never 403, so that it does not confirm the bond exists. | smoke |
